heading_en: Risk Weights of Qualifying STC Securitization Exposures
summary_ja: 適格STC証券化エクスポージャーのリスク・ウェイトの特例算出方法（内部格付手法準拠方式のパラメーター調整、外部格付・内部評価方式の読替え、標準的手法準拠方式のp=0.5）と、その適格要件二十二項目を定める。
summary_en: Provides preferential risk-weight calculations for qualifying STC (simple, transparent, comparable) securitization exposures under each method, with floors of 10% and 15%, and sets out the 22 qualifying requirements.
paragraphs: Where a qualifying STC securitization exposure falls under any of the following items, the risk weight of that qualifying STC securitization exposure may, notwithstanding Divisions 2 through 5, be calculated as prescribed in the relevant item; provided, however, that where the qualifying STC securitization exposure is a senior securitization exposure and its risk weight is less than 10%, the risk weight shall be 10%, and where it is not a senior securitization exposure and its risk weight is less than 15%, the risk weight shall be 15%. (i) where it is a securitization exposure for which the risk weight is calculated using the internal ratings-based approach-compliant method: Division 2 applies mutatis mutandis. In this case, notwithstanding the formula set out in Article 235, paragraph (1), the parameter (p) prescribed in that paragraph shall be the value calculated by the following formula. p = max[0.3, (A + B * (1 / N) + C * K_{IRB} + D * LGD + E * M_{T}) * 0.5] In this formula, K_{IRB} is as provided in Article 232, and N, LGD, M_{T}, A, B, C, D and E are as provided in Article 235; (ii) where it is a securitization exposure for which the risk weight is calculated using the external ratings-based approach-compliant method or the internal assessment approach: Division 3 or Division 4 applies mutatis mutandis, respectively. In this case, Article 236, paragraph (1) shall be read as follows according to the classification of cases set out in (a) through (c): (a) where the rating assigned by an eligible credit rating agency or an inferred rating (meaning the inferred rating prescribed in Article 237; the same applies in (b) and (c)) is a long-term rating and the securitization exposure is a senior securitization exposure: the term "{{T:p258t0}}" in Article 236, paragraph (1), item (i)(a) shall be read as "{{T:p258t1}}"; (b) where the rating assigned by an eligible credit rating agency or an inferred rating is a long-term rating and the securitization exposure is not a senior securitization exposure: the term "{{T:p259t1}}" in Article 236, paragraph (1), item (i)(b) shall be read as "{{T:p260t1}}"; (c) where the rating assigned by an eligible credit rating agency or an inferred rating is a short-term rating: the term "{{T:p261t0}}" in Article 236, paragraph (1), item (ii) shall be read as "{{T:p261t1}}"; (iii) where it is a securitization exposure for which the risk weight is calculated using the standardized approach-compliant method: Division 5 applies mutatis mutandis. In this case, the term "1 (provided, however, that for a re-securitization exposure it is 1.5)" in Article 241 shall be read as "0.5".
The preceding Division applies mutatis mutandis to the cases set out in the items of the preceding paragraph.

The term "qualifying STC securitization exposure" in paragraph (1) means an exposure relating to an asset-transfer securitization transaction (excluding the securitization exposures set out in the items of paragraph (2) of the following Article and re-securitization exposures) for which the originator and investors can confirm at all times that all of the following requirements are satisfied: (i) the characteristics of the original assets are homogeneous; (ii) investors can obtain information on loss experience (including delinquency status) for assets whose risk characteristics are substantially similar to those of the original assets, covering a period sufficient for investors to grasp the risk characteristics of the securitization transaction; (iii) the originator has the following number of years of experience in originating assets whose risk characteristics are substantially similar to those of the original assets, according to the classification of exposures in (a) or (b): (a) exposures to individuals or the like: five years or more; (b) exposures other than those set out in (a): seven years or more; (iv) at the time the original assets are included in the original asset pool, all of the following requirements are satisfied: (a) the original asset pool does not include receivables that are delinquent or in default or that show signs thereof; (b) the original asset pool does not include receivables for which parties to the securitization transaction are aware of evidence indicating a high probability of default, or receivables that are subject to attachment, provisional attachment or other compulsory execution proceedings; (v) the originator has, in principle, confirmed during the period from 45 days before the execution date of the securitization transaction through the execution date that none of the receivables constituting the original asset pool falls under any of (a) through (d): (a) the obligor has, during the three years preceding the origination of the receivable, been subject to a decision to commence bankruptcy proceedings, a decision to commence rehabilitation proceedings, a decision to commence reorganization proceedings, an order to commence special liquidation, or a decision to recognize foreign insolvency proceedings (including foreign proceedings equivalent to these), or a specified conciliation prescribed in Article 2, paragraph (3) of the Act on Specified Conciliation for Promoting the Adjustment of Specified Debts, etc. (Act No. 158 of 1999) has been concluded with respect to the obligor; (b) incident information concerning the obligor (meaning information from which a decline in the obligor's ability to pay can be inferred, such as delinquency, debt restructuring or subrogated payment) is registered with a public credit information agency; (c) where the obligor has been assigned a rating by an eligible credit rating agency or a similar external credit assessment, the obligor is assessed as having significantly high credit risk or as being in default; (d) a civil dispute has arisen between the original creditor (including the originator) and the obligor; (vi) at the time the receivables constituting the original asset pool are included in that pool, there has, in principle, been at least one repayment record for those receivables; (vii) the receivables constituting the original asset pool have been originated on the basis of the originator's consistent underwriting standards, without significant deterioration in creditworthiness and without significantly deteriorating the assets; (viii) the original assets have not been selected arbitrarily by the originator; (ix) the originator does not have effective control over the original assets, the original assets are legally isolated from the originator so that neither the originator nor its creditors can exercise control over them even in the originator's insolvency proceedings, etc., and an appropriate opinion from attorneys, etc. (excluding in-house counsel of the originator itself) has been obtained confirming this state of affairs; (x) investors can obtain, before the execution of the securitization transaction and during the term of the transaction, loan-level data on the original assets or, where the original asset pool is highly diversified, stratified data from which their risk characteristics can be grasped; (xi) redemption to investors in the securitization transaction does not depend on the sale or refinancing of the original assets; (xii) where interest rate risk or foreign exchange risk exists with respect to the payment of principal and interest, that risk is appropriately hedged and investors can obtain information on the hedging transactions; (xiii) the priority of payments of principal and interest is appropriately provided for in the related contracts, and information on the payment of principal and interest (including information on matters that may affect payments) is disclosed to investors before the execution of the transaction and during the term of the transaction; (xiv) all rights of the originator (including voting rights) relating to the individual original assets are transferred to the securitization special purpose entity upon the transfer of those original assets to it, and the rights held by investors are clearly provided for in the related contracts; (xv) investors can obtain, to the extent practicable, the appropriate transaction documents, or copies thereof, that have been confirmed by attorneys, etc. (excluding in-house counsel of the investor's own company) before the execution of the securitization transaction and during the term of the transaction; (xvi) the originator holds a portion of the securitization exposure in an appropriate manner (including satisfying any of the conditions set out in the items of Article 226, paragraph (3)); (xvii) the servicer of the securitization transaction satisfies all of the following requirements: (a) it has the ability to perform the entrusted business appropriately with a high level of expertise, and sufficient experience; (b) the transaction documents provide that the servicer has a duty to act so as not to harm the equitable treatment of the creditors of each tranche; (c) a fee structure corresponding to the content of the business is set; (xviii) the following matters are clearly stated in the transaction documents: (a) the contractual obligations and responsibilities of the related parties to the securitization transaction; (b) matters concerning the replacement of material related parties upon deterioration of their creditworthiness; (xix) investors can obtain the following information: (a) the payment record of principal and interest on the original assets (including scheduled payment amounts, prepaid principal amounts and accrued interest amounts); (b) the delinquency status, etc. of the original assets; (c) other information on the income and payments relating to the securitization transaction; (xx) as of the cut-off date of the original assets (meaning the reference date on which the original assets to be transferred to the securitization special purpose entity are determined; the same applies in the following item and in items (i) and (ii) of Article 245-4, paragraph (1)), the original assets are not commercial real estate-related exposures, and the risk weight of the original assets calculated pursuant to Chapter 3 (where the effects of credit risk mitigation techniques can be taken into account, the risk weight after taking those effects into account) satisfies the requirement prescribed in (a) through (c) below according to the type of original asset set out therein: (a) exposures to owner-occupied residential real estate, etc. or exposures to rental residential real estate: the risk weight obtained by taking the weighted average of the risk weights of the individual original assets by their amounts in the portfolio of original assets is 40% or less; (b) exposures to SMEs, etc. or retail exposures (excluding those falling under (a)): the risk weight of each individual original asset is 75% or less; (c) exposures other than those set out in (a) and (b): the risk weight of each individual original asset is 100% or less; (xxi) as of the cut-off date of the original assets, the ratio of the outstanding balance of each individual original asset receivable to the total outstanding balance of all receivables in the original asset pool is 1% or less (2% or less where all of the original assets are exposures to business corporations and the originator holds the most junior tranche of the securitization exposures in the securitization transaction and the total amount of that most junior tranche is 10% or more of the total amount of exposures of the original assets of the securitization transaction (including cases where the credit risk borne by the originator is equivalent thereto)); (xxii) under laws and regulations (including foreign laws and regulations) or contract, the originator is obliged to appropriately disclose to investors the information necessary to confirm, with respect to the securitization transaction, the requirements set out in the preceding items or requirements of the same kind in foreign jurisdictions.
